entries.name: pageBodyHtml
signatures: pageBodyHtml(page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel, heading: Bool) -> String
entries.summary: A page's content without the chrome — what `pageHtml` wraps in the layout, and what a host site (the fragments output) wraps in its own. `heading` is false when the host renders the title itself.

entries.name: submodulesHtml
entries.summary: A module family spread over several files ("Net" + net/dns.kex, net/http.kex, ...) gets one page per file, and the parent page says nothing about the rest — a reader on "Net" has no reason to believe Net.DNS or Net.Socket are documented at all. This section is the signpost: every descendant page, with the summary its module declares.

entries.name: submoduleItem
signatures: submoduleItem(child: SourcePage, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: preludeBodyHtml
signatures: preludeBodyHtml(page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel, heading: Bool) -> String
entries.summary: The prelude declares nothing, so the generic page renderer leaves it blank. What it HAS is a list of imports and a comment explaining them — which is exactly the page a reader wants: what am I given for free, and where does each of those live.

entries.name: preludeItem
signatures: preludeItem(model: PackageModel, fromPath: String, name: String) -> String

entries.name: preludeLink
signatures: preludeLink(model: PackageModel, fromPath: String, name: String) -> String
entries.summary:
A `using X` in prelude.kex names a sibling SOURCE FILE, so the page for that file is the exact target. Going through the link index instead would lose half the list: `Map`, `Set` and `Range` are ambiguous as bare names — a module and a type both claim them — and resolve to nothing.

The file is what matches, not the title: `using Test` is test.kex, whose page is titled "Assert", and `using Env` is env.kex, titled "ENV".

entries.name: versionIndexHtml
entries.summary: Landing page for <pkg>/<version>/index.html: every module as a card. When the package has a prelude, the cards are split by how a reader REACHES them — visible everywhere, or one `using` away — because that is the first question anyone has about a standard library.

entries.name: cardModules
entries.summary: The modules worth a card. `Int8`, `Float32` and friends are modules holding two constants each, declared in number.kex beside Integer and Float: listing them beside `Net` and `FS` made the index read as if the stdlib had a dozen integer libraries. They are on their file's page.

entries.name: preludePaths
entries.summary: The prelude imports FILES, and everything a listed file declares comes with it: `using Time` is what puts `Date`, `Duration` and `Time.Period` in scope, none of which prelude.kex names. So the split is by page, not by module name.

entries.name: latestVersion
entries.summary: The version a reader gets by default: the highest release by semantic version, never an unreleased `-dev` build while a release exists. versions.json is in BUILD order, newest build first, and tools/build-docs.sh builds the working tree last, so its first entry is usually the -dev build rather than the latest release.

entries.name: versionsNewestFirst
entries.summary: One package's versions, highest first by semantic version.

entries.name: packageRedirectHtml
entries.summary: <pkg>/index.html: straight on to the latest version, so a link to a package lands on its reference rather than on a list of builds. Every other version stays one click away, at versions.html.

entries.name: packageVersionsHtml
entries.summary: <pkg>/versions.html: the versions of one package, newest first — the page a reader lands on when they want a different release of what they are reading. What the ids MEAN is the package's own story: a library's own releases, the stdlib's Kex releases. The page does not need to know.

entries.name: searchPageHtml
entries.summary: <pkg>/<version>/search.html: the shareable full-page search. The modal on every page links here with ?q=<term>, so a results page is a URL rather than a state — the page reads the term back from the query string.

entries.name: rootIndexHtml
entries.summary: Site root index.html: one card per PACKAGE (its newest build), not per build — a reader arrives at "the docs" for a thing, and the thing is a package; its versions are one click down. Built from the accumulated versions.json entries, not just this build's model.

entries.name: packageNames
entries.summary: Package names in first-seen order of their newest entry: versions arrive newest-first from accumulateVersions, so the first entry of each package is that package's newest build.

entries.name: layout
signatures: layout(title: String, current: String, bodyContent: String, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: sidebar
entries.summary: The sidebar lists one entry per source FILE, nested by module family: a page whose title is a dotted child of another page's title nests under it ("Net.DNS" under "Net", "Net.HTTP.WebSocket" under "Net.HTTP"), so a multi-file module reads as one branch instead of trailing the list in directory-walk order. The active file expands to its top-level declarations so a reader can jump straight to one. The label is the page's title (the module it declares), not the raw file name. The heading is a link: it is the package's name, and the obvious thing to want from it is the list of what the package contains — which is the version index, where the prelude split lives.

entries.name: sidebarEntry
signatures: sidebarEntry(page: SourcePage, current: String, vpre: String, pages: [SourcePage]) -> String

entries.name: preludeTag
entries.summary: The page's own heading carries it — the sidebar is a list to scan, and a chip on 32 of 41 rows is noise rather than an answer.

entries.name: firstModulesOfPages
entries.summary: The modules that OPEN a page — their section sits at the very top, so a card for one links to the page itself rather than to an anchor that lands where the page already starts. A page whose first declaration is a type or record has no such module.

entries.name: entitiesHtml
signatures: entitiesHtml(entities: [Entity], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: A page's declarations in source order — except that a type's `make` blocks on the same page are pulled into the type's own section, so `List` reads as one thing (the type, then its methods, grouped by the receiver they need) rather than a type followed by three loose "make" sections.

entries.name: sectionEntities
entries.summary: The declarations that get a section of their own: everything except the make blocks folded into a type or trait on the same page.

entries.name: declaredTraitNames
entries.summary: A `make <Trait>` beside its trait is the trait's defaults, rendered in the trait's own section (Relations.traitMethods).

entries.name: entitySection
signatures: entitySection(e: Entity, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: linker
signatures: linker(page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String -> String

entries.name: hrefer
signatures: hrefer(page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String -> String
entries.summary: The bare href for a name, or "" — what linked highlighting and linked prose both need.

entries.name: typeSection
signatures: typeSection(e: TypeEntry, makes: [MakeEntry], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: variantsHtml
entries.summary: Only real constructors: an abstract type (`type List<X>`) has none, and a "Variants: (abstract)" heading told the reader nothing.

entries.name: recordSection
signatures: recordSection(e: RecordEntry, makes: [MakeEntry], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: typeBodyHtml
signatures: typeBodyHtml(name: String, makes: [MakeEntry], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: Everything about a type beyond its declaration: the traits it implements (from every file), its methods grouped by receiver, the methods it gets from those traits for free, and the other modules that add methods to it.

entries.name: makeGroupHtml
signatures: makeGroupHtml(m: MakeEntry, base: String, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: "Methods" for the plain receiver, "On `[Number]`" for a specialised one.

entries.name: genericReceiver?
entries.summary: `[X]` and `FileHandle<R, W>` are the type itself; `[Number]` is not.

entries.name: implementsHtml
signatures: implementsHtml(name: String, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: Every trait the type implements, wherever the implementing make block lives — algebra.kex is what makes Integer a Monoid, and number.kex's reader should still learn that.

entries.name: traitLinks
signatures: traitLinks(traits: [String], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: providedHtml
signatures: providedHtml(name: String, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: The trait methods a type gets without writing them: a trait's provided methods, minus any the type defines itself somewhere. This is the answer to "where does `List.eachIndexed` come from?".

entries.name: providedFromHtml
signatures: providedFromHtml(written: String, own: [String], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: elsewhereHtml
signatures: elsewhereHtml(name: String, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: Other modules that add methods to this type: `make Integer` in time.kex is where `5.seconds` comes from.

entries.name: linkTypeText
entries.summary: A type text is code with links inside it: split into identifier and punctuation segments, link the identifiers that resolve, escape the rest.

entries.name: linkType
signatures: linkType(links: [LinkEntry], fromPath: String, name: String) -> String
entries.summary: The whole-package resolution one segment goes through: an exact name hit links (display text escaped); anything else is plain escaped code.

entries.name: traitSection
signatures: traitSection(e: TraitEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: A trait: what an implementor must write, what it then gets for free, and who implements it.

entries.name: implementedByHtml
signatures: implementedByHtml(e: TraitEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: makeSection
signatures: makeSection(e: MakeEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: A make block with no type declaration on its page. On the type's home page (string.kex for String) it carries everything the type section would; elsewhere it points home.

entries.name: firstMakeOnPage?
signatures: firstMakeOnPage?(facts: Tey.Docgen.Model.TypeFacts, e: MakeEntry, page: SourcePage) -> Bool

entries.name: homeNote
signatures: homeNote(base: String, facts: Tey.Docgen.Model.TypeFacts?, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: moduleSection
signatures: moduleSection(e: ModuleEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: A module's own functions and constants are its API, listed under it (h3) like a type's methods. Types, traits and nested modules it declares stand as sections of their own after that.

entries.name: moduleMemberHtml
signatures: moduleMemberHtml(e: Entity, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: functionSection
signatures: functionSection(e: FunctionEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: constantSection
signatures: constantSection(e: ConstantEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: functionsHtml
signatures: functionsHtml(functions: [FunctionEntry], owner: String, level: Integer, implements: [String], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: Members of a trait or make block, one heading per NAME: overloads (`count` and `count(pred)`) are one method with several signatures, not two unrelated entries. `owner` scopes the anchors; `implements` lets a member that fulfils a trait method say which trait.

entries.name: functionGroupHtml
signatures: functionGroupHtml(fs: [FunctionEntry], name: String, owner: String, level: Integer, implements: [String], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: traitTag
signatures: traitTag(name: String, implements: [String], page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: "from Enumerable": this member is the type's own version of a method the trait declares, linked to the trait's description of it.

entries.name: overloadHtml
signatures: overloadHtml(f: FunctionEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: One overload: its signature first (what you call), then the prose.

entries.name: signaturesHtml
signatures: signaturesHtml(f: FunctionEntry, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: docHtml
signatures: docHtml(doc: Doc, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String

entries.name: entityDocHtml
signatures: entityDocHtml(doc: Doc, page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: A declaration's doc: prose, then its examples and any deprecation — a type's @example is as much a part of it as a method's.

entries.name: plainDocHtml
entries.summary: Unlinked: for prose with no page to resolve against (the prelude comment, card summaries).

entries.name: summaryParagraphs
entries.summary: Paragraphs break on blank lines — except inside a fenced block, where a blank line is part of the code rather than the end of a paragraph.

entries.name: paragraphHtml
entries.summary: A summary paragraph is prose, a fenced block that Rdoc produced from an indented (verbatim) block, or a bullet list — each rendered as what it is rather than reflowed into one paragraph.

entries.name: bulletListHtml
entries.summary: `- item` lines, with indented continuation lines folded into the item above them.

entries.name: inlineCode
entries.summary: Minimal inline Markdown for doc prose: `code` spans. Splitting on the backtick alternates plain/code segments; an unmatched trailing backtick degrades to literal text rather than swallowing the rest of the page.

entries.name: linkedInline
entries.summary: The same, with a code span that names something documented — a type, a trait, `List.map` — linked to it.

entries.name: linkableCode?
entries.summary: Only a bare name is a reference: `List`, `FS.Path`, `List.map`. A code span with spaces or parentheses is an expression, not a name.

entries.name: paramsHtml
signatures: paramsHtml(f: FunctionEntry, link: (String -> String), page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: Each parameter's meaning. Its type is in the signature right above, so it is repeated here only when there is no signature to read it from.

entries.name: returnsHtml
signatures: returnsHtml(f: FunctionEntry, link: (String -> String), page: SourcePage, model: PackageModel) -> String
entries.summary: The signature already states the result type, so when there is one "Returns" says only what the value MEANS. A @return tag whose type disagrees would otherwise put two answers side by side (`min : X?` above "Returns: Number?").

entries.name: esc
entries.summary: Escape text for HTML (content and double-quoted attributes).

entries.name: pageTarget
entries.summary: The page the version switcher tries first in the target version.

entries.name: markdownLink
entries.summary: Every page's raw Markdown, next to its HTML: the footer link humans see, and the address llms.txt tells models about. Index pages have none. The target is a bare sibling filename — the page already stands in the directory its `.md` was written to, so no prefix climbing is wanted.

entries.name: versionPrefix
entries.summary: Relative path from a page's urlPath back to the version directory: "string" → "" (sibling), "kex/ast" → "../".

entries.name: rootPrefix
entries.summary: From the page to the site root: version dir is <pkg>/<version>/.

signatures: writePages(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> Integer
writeHtml(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()

entries.name: externalLinks
entries.summary: Names another unit documents, so this one's signatures and prose can link to them: the Tey reference links `String` and `FS.Path` into the standard library's. Each model.json says which unit it is; its pages sit at ../../<package>/<version>/ from this unit's version directory. A file that cannot be read is reported and skipped — links are an extra.

entries.name: writeUnitIndexFiles
entries.summary: The unit's own index files — its manifest and the shared versions.json — without the site-level ones (landing pages, llms.txt, sitemap), which a host site that frames fragments owns.

entries.name: reportDocDrift
entries.summary: A @return tag that names a different type than the signature declares is a doc comment that has drifted from its code (`min : X?` documented as returning `Number?`). The page shows the signature's type; this says where the tag disagrees so the comment can be fixed.

entries.name: preludeInfo
entries.summary:
A source tree with a `prelude.kex` has a subset that is visible without an import, and the reader wants to know which. The file is declarative by convention — an opening comment, then one bare `using <Module>` per line — so reading it is enough. A package without one gets empties, and nothing in the output mentions a prelude at all.

Returns (the file, the modules it makes visible, its opening comment).

entries.name: leadingComment
entries.summary: The file's opening comment block, `#` markers stripped, ready for the same Rdoc parse every other doc comment goes through.

entries.name: fileHeader
entries.summary: The file's opening comment, when it is its own block: a blank line after it, not a declaration. A comment that runs straight into a declaration is that declaration's doc, and the page gets no intro.

entries.name: usingName
entries.summary: "using List" -> "List"; anything else (a comment, a blank line, an `only:` list) -> "".

entries.name: defaultSource
entries.summary: `src/` when it is standing there, else the flag as given (an empty one is reported by the scan: "no .kex files found in").

entries.name: defaultPackage
entries.summary: The manifest's name when the CWD is a package — the identity docgen should not have to be told. Outside one, "": the caller has to say, and buildCommand refuses rather than inventing a name. Docgen used to answer "prelude" here, which meant a build with a swallowed or forgotten --package filed its pages under whatever the CWD's package.kex said (the stdlib was published as "kex" for exactly that reason, kexhq/kex#287).

entries.name: defaultVersion
entries.summary: The version of the thing being documented: a package's own release when standing in one. What a package's versions ARE differs per package — a library's own releases, the stdlib's Kex releases — so outside a package this is the caller's to state (--release) rather than docgen's to guess.

entries.name: manifestVersion
entries.summary: (name, version) of the package.kex in the CWD, if there is a readable one. Both defaults read it; one read, one parse.

signatures: writePages(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> Integer

entries.name: writeHtml
signatures: writeHtml(pages: [SourcePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
entries.summary: HTML mirrors the Markdown layout: one page per source file, plus the version landing page, the site-root redirect and the shared stylesheet.

entries.name: dirNameOf
entries.summary: "kex/ast" → "kex"; "fs" → "" (already inside versionDir).

entries.name: versionManifestJson
entries.summary: One version's pages, with the package and version they belong to, so a reader of the file needs nothing but the file. Page paths stay relative to the version directory — the URL prefix is `<package>/<version>/`, and whoever assembles the site is the one that knows the site root.

entries.name: accumulateVersions
entries.summary: The output directory is the published site, so a build must not clobber the versions other builds published: read what is there, upsert this (package, version), write the union back, newest first.

entries.name: upsertVersion
entries.summary: This build's entry first, the other packages' and versions' kept: the pure half of accumulate, so the upsert rule itself can be spec'd.

entries.name: fieldValues
entries.summary: A named helper so the lambda's element type comes from the [FieldEntry] parameter, not from the surrounding map literal's value type.

entries.name: entityTypes
entries.summary: The type names an entity is "about" — the search-by-type dimension. For a function that is its signature's types; for a record its field types; for a type its parents and variant fields; for a trait/make the types its methods mention; for a module the union of its children.

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Md
signatures: assign(front: Frontmatter, key: String, value: String) -> Frontmatter
wrap(text: String, strongMark: String, strongTag: String, emMark: String, emTag: String) -> String

indexOfText(haystack: String, needle: String, at: Integer) -> Integer?

entries.name: Frontmatter
entries.summary: A document's frontmatter: the keys the prose pipeline reads. Unknown keys are parsed and ignored rather than rejected, so a page can carry metadata a later renderer will use.

entries.name: ListItem
entries.summary: One item of a list: its own inline text, plus any blocks nested under it.

entries.name: parseDocument
entries.summary: The whole job: text in, document out.

entries.name: toHtml
entries.summary: Text in, HTML out — `parse` then `render`, which is all a caller wanting a page body needs.

entries.name: splitFrontmatter
entries.summary:
--- frontmatter -------------------------------------------------------

A leading `---` fence delimits frontmatter. Without one the document is all body, and every field takes its default.

entries.name: assign
signatures: assign(front: Frontmatter, key: String, value: String) -> Frontmatter

entries.name: trimEnds
entries.summary: Drops the first and last character — the quotes `quoted?` just matched.

entries.name: blockLoop
entries.summary: One pass over the lines, each branch consuming the whole construct it recognises and returning the lines it did not take.

entries.name: rule?
entries.summary: `---`, `***` or `___`, three or more, nothing else on the line. Checked after frontmatter is gone, so a stray `---` here really is a break.

entries.name: headingLevel
entries.summary: `##` → 2. Zero when the line is not a heading; `#hashtag` is not one.

entries.name: takeCode
entries.summary:
--- fenced code -------------------------------------------------------

The info string is the language. An unterminated fence runs to the end of the document rather than failing — a truncated page still renders.

entries.name: takeQuote
entries.summary:
--- blockquotes -------------------------------------------------------

`>` is stripped from each line and what remains is parsed as blocks, so a quote can hold anything a document can, nesting included.

entries.name: takeList
entries.summary:
--- lists -------------------------------------------------------------

Nesting is by indentation: a line indented past the first item's marker belongs to that item and is parsed as blocks in its own right, so a list can hold paragraphs, code and deeper lists.

entries.name: listLine?
entries.summary: A list continues through its own items, indented continuation lines, and blank lines — but a blank line followed by unindented text ends it, which is why the run is cut at the first line that is neither.

entries.name: flushItem
entries.summary: The first line is the item's own text; anything below it is nested content, dedented so it parses as a document of its own.

entries.name: dedent
entries.summary: Removes the common indent, so nested content is parsed at column zero.

entries.name: numberMarker
entries.summary: "12. " → "12." ; anything else → "".

entries.name: tableStart?
entries.summary:
--- tables ------------------------------------------------------------

A GFM table is a header row and a delimiter row of dashes; without the delimiter the lines are ordinary paragraphs.

entries.name: cellsOf
entries.summary: Leading and trailing pipes are optional, so the split is trimmed of the empty cells they produce.

entries.name: takeParagraph
entries.summary:
--- paragraphs --------------------------------------------------------

Runs to a blank line or to the start of any other construct, so a list or fence directly under prose is not swallowed into it.

entries.name: renderCode
entries.summary: Kex code goes through the same highlighter the reference pages use, so a snippet in the guide looks like a signature in the reference. Everything else is escaped and left plain.

entries.name: anchor
entries.summary: A heading's id: lowercase, non-alphanumerics folded to single dashes.

entries.name: trimDashes
entries.summary: `String.trim` takes no argument, and the folding above can leave a dash at either end (`## \`try\`` → `-try-`).

entries.name: stripInline
entries.summary: Inline markers removed, for anchors and any other plain-text use.

entries.name: inline
entries.summary:
--- inline ------------------------------------------------------------

Code spans first and separately: their content is escaped but never scanned for emphasis, so `a*b*c` inside backticks stays literal.

entries.name: emphasis
entries.summary: Links before emphasis, so a `*` inside a URL is not read as a marker.

entries.name: linkParts
entries.summary: `label](href)` → (label, href, what follows). None when the shape is not a link after all, in which case the `[` is literal text.

entries.name: marks
entries.summary: `**bold**` before `*italic*`, or the opening `**` would parse as an empty emphasis. Escaping happens here, on the text that is left.

entries.name: wrap
signatures: wrap(text: String, strongMark: String, strongTag: String, emMark: String, emTag: String) -> String

entries.name: pairs
signatures: pairs(text: String, mark: String, tag: String, accum: String) -> String
entries.summary: Replaces each surviving pair of markers with a tag. An unpaired marker is left as written rather than swallowing the rest of the line.

entries.name: indexOfText
signatures: indexOfText(haystack: String, needle: String, at: Integer) -> Integer?
entries.summary: Where `needle` first occurs in `haystack`, or None. String.indexOf takes a Char, and the markers here are two characters wide ("**"), so the search is spelled out.

entries.name: Extension
entries.summary: One `make` block seen from the type it extends: where it is, what it adds, and which traits it declares. A type's methods are spread over many files (`make Integer` lives in number.kex, time.kex, units.kex and algebra.kex), and these rows are what put them back together.

entries.name: TypeFacts
entries.summary: Everything the package says about one type, across files. `homePath` is the page a reader should land on for the type — the one declaring it, or the one named after it for builtins such as Integer and String.

entries.name: TraitFacts
entries.summary: A trait seen from the outside: where it is documented and which make blocks implement it.

entries.name: ModuleIndexEntry
entries.summary: The navigation unit: one per module in the package, pointing at the page its entities live on. The sidebar and the module index of model.json are built from these — a FILE is where source lives, a MODULE is what a reader navigates by, and the two only coincide by accident.

entries.name: MemberEntry
entries.summary: One documented member of a module, with the anchor its section renders at — the sidebar's expanded list and the JSON index both use these.

entries.name: LinkEntry
entries.summary: One row of the cross-link index: a name a type reference elsewhere in the package may mention ("String", "FS.Path") and where it lands. The index is what makes interlinked docs possible without per-renderer guesswork: every renderer resolves names against the same list.

entries.name: SearchEntry
entries.summary: A flattened search row: one per entity (and per function inside traits, makes and modules), joining name/kind/signature to the page URL. The `types` are the type names the entity is about — the types its signature mentions — so search can answer by name AND by type; `anchor` is the section id a result deep-links to.

entries.name: VersionEntry
entries.summary: One row of versions.json. The file accumulates across builds — the output directory IS the site, so each build upserts its (package, id) entry into whatever is already published there.

entries.name: kindOf
entries.summary: The kind label used in indexes and JSON for each entity variant.

entries.name: nameOf
entries.summary: The primary display name of an entity (a make's is its target type).

entries.name: anchorOf
entries.summary: The anchor id an entity's HTML section renders at. Lives here — not in the HTML renderer — because the cross-link index and the sidebar compute the same ids, and the HTML must match whatever they resolved to.

entries.name: anchorNameOf
entries.summary: A make's anchor is keyed by its full target spelling (type params included), a module's by its qualified name — the section ids are derived from the same texts.

entries.name: memberAnchorOf
entries.summary: The anchor of a function documented inside a trait or make section: scoped by its owner, because `count` is a member of both `[X]` and `String`, and one page can hold several owners.

entries.name: ownerSlugOf
entries.summary: An owner spelled as a type: `[X]` -> "list", `[Number]` -> "list-number", `FileHandle<CanRead, W>` -> "filehandle-canread". Type variables (a lone capital, optionally numbered) say nothing about WHICH methods these are, so they are dropped rather than baked into every anchor.

entries.name: wordsOf
entries.summary: Identifier-ish runs of a type text: letters, digits, `_`, `?`, `!`.

entries.name: slugOf
entries.summary: An id-safe spelling of a name: lower case, every run of punctuation one dash. `?` and `!` survive — they are part of Kex names (`empty?`) and legal in a fragment.

entries.name: operatorSlug
entries.summary: An operator method has no letters to slug: `+` is "op-plus", `<=>` is "op-lt-eq-gt" — distinct, stable and readable in a URL.

entries.name: baseTypeOf
entries.summary: "[X]" -> "List", "{K: V}" -> "Map", "FileHandle<R, W>" -> "FileHandle", "Map<K, V>" -> "Map": the type a make block extends, whatever specialisation it spells.

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Nav
signatures: claimedByAnother?(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage, title: String) -> Bool
memberLinks(ownerName: String, owner: String, functions: [Tey.Docgen.Model.FunctionEntry], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
splitLoop(rest: String, ident: String, sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
hrefFrom(fromPath: String, toPath: String, anchor: String) -> String

entries.name: buildModules
entries.summary: Every module in the package, in declaration order, pointing at the page it lives on. Nested modules are entries of their own (the sidebar nests them by name).

entries.name: parentTitleOf
entries.summary: The file tree a module family grows into, rebuilt from titles: a page nests under the page whose title is its dotted prefix, so "Net.DNS" (net/dns.kex) is a child of "Net" (net.kex), and "Net.HTTP.WebSocket" of "Net.HTTP". The longest existing prefix wins; a prefix with no page of its own ("Control" for "Control.Retry") leaves the page at the top level. Titles, not paths, carry the relation — the module names are what a reader scans for.

entries.name: claimedByAnother?
signatures: claimedByAnother?(pages: [SourcePage], page: SourcePage, title: String) -> Bool

entries.name: topLevelPages
entries.summary: The sidebar's top level: pages nothing parents, alphabetically by title — a reader scans by name, not by directory-walk order.

entries.name: childPages
entries.summary: The pages nested directly under `title`, alphabetically.

entries.name: descendantPages
entries.summary: Every page in `page`'s family at any depth, alphabetically — what a module page lists as its submodules.

entries.name: buildLinks
entries.summary: Linkable names, unique-target-wins: a name links while exactly one (page, anchor) answers it. A qualified name ("FS.Path") is its own name; a simple one ("Path") survives only while nothing else claims it — once two different entities answer "Request", the simple spelling stops linking and only the spelled-out names do.

entries.name: withTypeHomes
entries.summary: The links, plus a home for every type that make blocks extend. A bare `Integer` is claimed by a module (number parsing) AND by five make blocks, so the uniqueness rule drops it — yet a type name in a signature means the type, and the type has a home page (Relations.homePathOf). Those homes fill in what uniqueness left out; a name that already links keeps its link.

entries.name: memberLinks
signatures: memberLinks(ownerName: String, owner: String, functions: [Tey.Docgen.Model.FunctionEntry], urlPath: String) -> [LinkEntry]
entries.summary: `List.map`, `Enumerable.filter`: members are linkable under their owner's name, so prose that writes `List.map` lands on the method.

entries.name: linkableNames
entries.summary: A type/reference name links under its qualified name; entities whose qualified name is the bare name (top-level declarations) offer that spelling too. A make's target with type parameters ("[X]", "Map<K, V>") links under the base name before the "<" — the anchor is still the full-target one, matching the section id.

entries.name: uniqueTarget?
entries.summary: Whether `candidate`'s name answers to exactly one target: every other entry under the same name must land on the same (page, anchor).

entries.name: segmentsOf
entries.summary: Splits a type reference into identifier segments and separator runs, so a renderer can link the identifiers and leave the punctuation alone: "Map<String, FS.Path>" → ["Map", "<", "String", ", ", "FS.Path", ">"].

entries.name: splitLoop
signatures: splitLoop(rest: String, ident: String, sep: String, out: [String]) -> [String]
entries.summary: `ident` is the identifier being read, `sep` the separator run since it; only one is non-empty at a time, and whichever it is goes out in order.

entries.name: hrefFrom
signatures: hrefFrom(fromPath: String, toPath: String, anchor: String) -> String
entries.summary: The href from one page of this package to another, with anchor: same page → "#anchor"; else up to the version directory and back down.

nextLink(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, up: String) -> String

entries.name: ProsePage
entries.summary: A page and the things only its frontmatter knows: where it sorts, the HTML its Markdown became, the description its index entry shows, and the Markdown (minus frontmatter) its raw `.md` rendering serves.

entries.name: writeProse
signatures: writeProse(pages: [ProsePage], versionDir: String, out: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()
entries.summary: Both renderings, from the same parsed page: HTML for readers, Markdown for crawlers, LLMs, and the "Markdown" link every page carries — the same `.md`-next-to-`.html` pairing reference builds write.

entries.name: writeProseLoop
signatures: writeProseLoop(pages: [ProsePage], index: Integer, versionDir: String, model: PackageModel) -> ()

entries.name: proseIndexHtml
entries.summary: The book's own spine: chapters in author order with their descriptions, not the module grid reference builds get. Deliberately separate from `versionIndexHtml` — `tey docs build` keeps documenting any package, and nothing about a book leaks into it.

entries.name: prevNextHtml
entries.summary: Chapter footer: the siblings around this one, so the book reads forward as well as sideways. First and last chapters link one way only.

entries.name: Tey.Docgen.Rdoc
signatures: plusPair?(head: String, inner: String, tail: String) -> Bool
classifyBlocks(blocks: [[String]], summary: String, params: [Param], returns: Return?, examples: [Example], deprecated: String?) -> Doc?
findClosingBracket(s: String, index: Integer, depth: Integer) -> Integer?

entries.name: rewriteProseBlocks
entries.summary: ``code`` is prose markup, so it is rewritten per prose block — after the split, not before it. Rewriting the whole comment at once paired a `+` operator inside an indented code sample (say `1 + 1`) with the next prose pair (``describe``), turning the operator into a stray backtick and eating the markup. Verbatim blocks and `@example` code are Kex source and are left alone; `@param`/`@return` descriptions are prose and still rewrite. Pairing never crosses a block: each block is rewritten on its own.

entries.name: plusPair?
signatures: plusPair?(head: String, inner: String, tail: String) -> Bool
entries.summary: A ``...`` pair is markup only when it reads as one: content with no space against either delimiter (so `1 + 1` stays an addition), no backtick inside (so converted spans never nest), and a non-identifier character on both sides (so `a+b` stays put even if it ever reaches here).

entries.name: splitParagraphs
entries.summary: Splits lines into paragraphs (blocks). Prose groups until a blank line; directives are LINE-based, so each `@param`/`@return`/`@example` line begins its own paragraph — consecutive `@param a` / `@param b` lines must not merge into one block, or only the first would be parsed. An `@example`'s indented code lines follow it and stay in its block (they do not open with `@`).

entries.name: indentWidth
entries.summary:
RDoc's verbatim marker is indentation: a prose block whose every line is indented is code — or a hand-laid-out table — that the author positioned deliberately. Reflowing it into a paragraph loses both the line breaks and the highlighting, so it is carried through the summary as a fenced block instead, which both renderers turn back into a highlighted `<pre>`.

Leading-space count of a line.

entries.name: dedent
entries.summary: Strips the common indentation shared by every non-blank line, so a block written at two spaces (or nested deeper) renders flush left.

entries.name: mergeVerbatim
entries.summary: A blank line inside a verbatim block ends a paragraph but not the block, so adjacent verbatim blocks are re-joined with the blank line between them.

entries.name: classifyBlocks
signatures: classifyBlocks(blocks: [[String]], summary: String, params: [Param], returns: Return?, examples: [Example], deprecated: String?) -> Doc?

entries.name: parseReturn
entries.summary: Reads a `@return [Type] description` directive.

entries.name: parseBracketed
entries.summary: "[...]" prefix → Bracketed. None when the text does not open with a bracketed group.

entries.name: findClosingBracket
signatures: findClosingBracket(s: String, index: Integer, depth: Integer) -> Integer?

signatures: extensionOf(page: SourcePage, entity: Entity, entry: MakeEntry) -> Extension
homeAnchorOf(base: String, home: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String
namesTrait?(written: String, name: String, qualifiedName: String) -> Bool

entries.name: extensionOf
signatures: extensionOf(page: SourcePage, entity: Entity, entry: MakeEntry) -> Extension

entries.name: homePathOf
entries.summary: Where a reader should land for a type: the page declaring it; else the page titled after it (string.kex for the builtin String); else the page whose make block adds the most methods — number.kex for Integer, not algebra.kex, which only makes it a Monoid.

entries.name: homeAnchorOf
signatures: homeAnchorOf(base: String, home: String, mine: [Extension], pages: [SourcePage]) -> String

entries.name: namesTrait?
signatures: namesTrait?(written: String, name: String, qualifiedName: String) -> Bool
entries.summary: `implement: Enumerable` and `implement: Kex.Enumerable` both name the trait declared as `Enumerable` inside `module Kex`.

entries.name: typeFactsFor
entries.summary: The facts for the type a make target extends, if any make extends it.

entries.name: traitEntryFor
entries.summary: The declaration of a trait, for its method list.

entries.name: traitMethods
entries.summary: A trait's methods as an implementor sees them. Required: declared with no body and given no default anywhere. Provided: a body in the trait, or a default from a `make <Trait>` block in any file — plus methods such a block adds that the trait never declared.

entries.name: traitTarget?
entries.summary: Whether a make target names a trait of this package.

entries.name: allFunctions
entries.summary: Every function documented anywhere in these entities: top-level and module functions, trait methods, make members.

entries.name: required?
entries.summary: A trait method with no clause is one an implementor must write; one with a body comes for free.

entries.name: proseFiles
entries.summary: The prose half of the same walk: `tey docs prose` reads .md rather than .kex, and wants the same recursion, the same sorting and the same skip.

entries.name: routesFor
entries.summary: The URL paths a browser would type for this file: an index.html is reached by its directory ("/", "/prelude/0.4.0-alpha/") as much as by its name, and the router matches exactly — so it answers the bare, the slash-terminated, and the named spelling. Every other file answers its own path only.
